Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L04_GuidedPractice_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.10

Which sentence uses the clearest academic language during speech feedback?

answer.text: A. Your speech had good stuff in it.

feedback.text: This is too vague. Academic language should name the specific communication skill or speech part.

answer.text: B. It sounded okay, I guess.

feedback.text: This is vague and uncertain. It does not help the speaker understand what to keep or improve.

answer.text: C. The thing you said was nice.

feedback.text: This does not identify the speech element or explain why it was effective.

answer.text: D. Your evidence supports the main claim clearly.

feedback.text: Correct. This uses precise academic vocabulary and explains what worked in the speech.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L04_GuidedPractice_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.05

Which word is the best academic replacement for "stuff" in a speech discussion?

answer.text: A. things

feedback.text: This is still vague. It does not name the specific information being discussed.

answer.text: B. evidence

feedback.text: Correct. Evidence is a precise academic word for information used to support a claim.

answer.text: C. something

feedback.text: This is also vague. Academic language should be more precise.

answer.text: D. whatever

feedback.text: This is informal and does not clarify meaning.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L04_GuidedPractice_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.10

Which feedback best explains a communication issue?

answer.text: A. The transition between your first and second reason needs to be clearer.

feedback.text: Correct. This names the issue and points to a specific place in the speech.

answer.text: B. The middle was weird.

feedback.text: This is vague and does not explain what should improve.

answer.text: C. It was not good there.

feedback.text: This does not identify the problem or the location clearly.

answer.text: D. You should talk better.

feedback.text: This is too general to help the speaker revise.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L04_GuidedPractice_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which response uses academic language while still supporting collaboration?

answer.text: A. Your part is bad, and mine is better.

feedback.text: This attacks the classmate and does not support collaboration.

answer.text: B. I do not like it, so change everything.

feedback.text: This gives an opinion but not academic feedback.

answer.text: C. Your claim is clear; we could add evidence so the audience understands it better.

feedback.text: Correct. This uses academic language, gives respectful feedback, and suggests a collaborative improvement.

answer.text: D. I will fix it myself because you cannot.

feedback.text: This is disrespectful and removes collaboration.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L04_GuidedPractice_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.10

Which statement best explains the purpose of academic language in oral communication?

answer.text: A. It makes the speaker sound more complicated.

feedback.text: This is a misconception. Academic language should clarify meaning, not make speech harder to understand.

answer.text: B. It helps the audience understand precise ideas clearly.

feedback.text: Correct. Academic language uses exact words so listeners can follow the speaker's meaning.

answer.text: C. It replaces the need for examples.

feedback.text: This is incorrect. Academic language and examples can work together to support understanding.

answer.text: D. It allows speakers to avoid explaining their ideas.

feedback.text: This is the opposite of the lesson concept. Academic language should support explanation.
